preregistered.written_before: the planner. scripts/step4_prereg.py refuses to run once plan.json exists; site.json and the world snapshot site_c.before are the only artefacts that predate this file.

site.surface: terracotta badlands -- terracotta 138, red_sand 53, banded orange/red/yellow/white terracotta 43, water 22 (of 260 sampled columns)
site.why: The spec asks for a usable base or rim plus a tall continuous face, and none of relief, std or mean slope measures that. scripts/step4_site_probe.py measures it directly: the height gained over a 12-block run in each cardinal direction, connected into faces; and level ground as connected columns whose 5x5 neighbourhood spans <=3 blocks. On those numbers this site is the only escarpment in the field. It has 9,431 face columns in one connected face 192 wide, a rim shelf of 14,187 level columns at y=123 and a base shelf of 4,782 at y=62, and the scarp between them is continuous from z=1164 to z=1338 -- every 6-block section of it drops 40-46 blocks over 13 to 53 horizontal, i.e. a grade of 0.75 to 3.23. (1536,-1536) has more relief spread over the whole site with no single face: it is a fifth rolling hillside, which the spec says tells us almost nothing. (-1152,-384) has std 5.2 -- one deep hole in flat ground. (1536,384) is 58% ocean with no level rim. (-1536,1536) is dunes: its best face gains 20.
site.the_face: the rim plateau lies west and southwest at y 118-129; the base plain lies east and southeast at y 68-78, falling to water in the southeast corner; between them one sinuous scarp running roughly north-south through the middle of the site. The steepest usable stretch is z 1256-1302 at x -1090..-1050: 40-44 blocks of drop in 19-25 horizontal.
site.spec_escape_clause_not_taken: The spec allows taking the highest-relief site and building what the terrain allows if nothing has a real face. It does. This is a badlands escarpment and the settlement is sited on it.
site.evidence: out/step4_sites.json, out/step4_probe/, out/site_c/site.json; commands: bash scripts/mcrun.sh scripts/step4_site_probe.py, bash scripts/mcrun.sh scripts/step4_site_dump.py, ETHOSLM_SETTLEMENT=site_c bash scripts/mcrun.sh scripts/prepare_settlement.py -1152 1152 192

voice.name: cut_sandstone_terraces
voice.why: Chosen rather than left to the planner, to spend the run's one degree of freedom on the settlement and not on the palette. styles.VOICES describes it as dry-country cut stone, 'everything stepping up the hill in terraces', ground 'terraced hard, retaining walls doubling as the walls of the storey below', signature 'an external stair climbing the outside of the building to its roof'. That is a description of the settlement in the spec's section 3, written before the spec was, and sandstone on banded terracotta is the Bandiagara/Mesa Verde pairing the spec names. The planner may adjust the palette within the voice.

check2_judgement.primary_question: does the staged pipeline produce a settlement that reads as human-made?
check2_judgement.operationalised_as: stages.QUESTION_ELEVATION). No new judge question is invented for this run.
check2_judgement.question: Which of these two buildings is better made? A or B, one sentence.
check2_judgement.pairing_rule: Frozen here, before any structure exists. Take both towns' plots.json; merge plots sharing a label into the union of their rectangles; drop any plot with no built blocks inside it; sort each town's list by footprint area descending; pair rank against rank; truncate to min(N_round8, N_round7). Deterministic, computed from disk, uses no judgement.
check2_judgement.cards:
the E1d shot list, matched between the two towns: eye-level from the lane at the
reserved door, close three-quarter from NE and SW, one NE aerial, composed into one 2x2
card per building at 900x560 spp 40.

floor.rule: wins > losses over the N pairs
floor.why_this_rule: a rate threshold with ties counting against is not robust to a tie rate the project has measured at 15-31%: a genuinely better town can score 45/40/15 and 'fail' a 50% bar on noise. wins > losses is the parity statement that survives the measured noise floor, and it is registered before any number exists.

also_reported_registered_in_advance: win rate with ties counting against
tie rate -- the noise floor, informative every time it has been reported
check2_judgement.confound:
RECORDED IN ADVANCE AND LOAD-BEARING. E3 established that terrain differences dominate
settlement-scale comparisons, so a whole-town-versus-whole-town verdict is close to
meaningless and MUST NOT be the headline; no such comparison is run. Even per building,
a win here is not attributable to the split pipeline alone -- step 3's same-site arm
comparison is the only clean evidence for that, and it is already on the record. What
this check can establish is whether the staged pipeline's output holds up against the
project's previous best under a judge validated for craft at constant terrain (E-craft,
4/4 with a blind human).

check3_goodhart.question: do the previewer's verdicts agree with Chunky's on the same pairs? If they disagree, builders have been optimising for the previewer rather than for the world.
check3_goodhart.pairs: the SAME N pairs as check 2, by the same frozen pairing rule. No pair is added, dropped or reordered between the two checks.
check3_goodhart.agreement: verdicts are three-way (a / b / tie) and agreement is exact equality. Both instruments are position-swapped, both blinded, both cached.

threshold.decision_rule: agreement >= 0.70 -- the previewer may carry massing selection, and select becomes a candidate arm for a later round. agreement < 0.70 -- the previewer stays an inner-loop design instrument, select stays off, and the calibration loop (Chunky as reference, previewer improved until it agrees) is the named prerequisite.
threshold.why_0.70: chance agreement on three-way verdicts is about 1/3; the previewer scored 45-53% on the damage task the judge passes at ground truth. 0.70 is the level at which the cheap instrument would be carrying more signal than noise on a decision that costs a build. Registered before any pair is rendered.

also_reported_registered_in_advance: agreement over the pairs where BOTH instruments were decisive
each instrument's own tie rate on these pairs
the pairs where they disagree, named, with both reasons quoted
check3_goodhart.confound: the two cards are not the same picture. The Chunky card is four path-traced shots including an eye-level approach; the preview card is an isometric and an elevation. This measures the cheap instrument against ground truth AS EACH IS ACTUALLY USED, which is the decision-relevant comparison, and not 'one framing, two renderers'. A disagreement therefore does not by itself convict the renderer rather than the shot list.

plots_are_2d_rectangles.question: did any planned structure have to move because plots cannot overlap in 2-D?
answered_with: every reserve() that returned False, recorded to out/site_c/plot_conflicts.json by the registry as it happens
per structure, the offset between the planner's footprint in plan.json and the rectangle actually claimed in plots.json, and any planned structure with no plot at all
the count of built columns that lie vertically above or below another structure's claimed plot -- the direct test of whether two dwellings on one cliff face can both claim their ground
plots_are_2d_rectangles.expected: failure is an expected outcome to be recorded, not a risk to be avoided. Hierarchy and scale sit on this abstraction and the next round needs its shape.

circulation_routes_the_climb.question: did circulation route the climb, and at what grade?
answered_with: is the network one connected component (E007), and is the lowest reserved threshold reachable from the highest by observe.Nav flood
the rise between the lowest and the highest reserved threshold
the maximum single-step rise along the lane, and the count of stair cells laid
the fraction of planned structures whose reserved threshold is on the network (W005)
circulation_routes_the_climb.expected: circulation is a walkable surface network and a 40-block climb is at the edge of what it can route. Record exactly how it fails if it fails.
